semanticChecks.method: Self-reviewed every Indonesian and Tagalog field directly against the canonical Japanese; no peer translations read.
semanticChecks.fullText: All titles, paragraphs, prompts, key terms and illustration alt text translated without summaries.
semanticChecks.conditionsNegationsUncertainty: Preserved absent/unreceived/unconfirmed documents, non-universal product capabilities, may-dispersal uncertainty, and the inability to infer whole-system suitability from appearance or equipment availability.
semanticChecks.technicalDistinctions: Retained ladder travel versus work platform, leaning angle versus upper/lower support, folding ladder versus convertible ladder and step stool, handhold versus railing, mobile scaffold versus transport cart, component delivery versus assembly approval, work-platform height versus reach height and training category, sweeping versus collection, visible cleanliness versus airborne contamination, and blowing versus suction/dust collection.
semanticChecks.numbers: Numeric tokens match the source field-by-field; Japanese word counts translated as words, not digits.
semanticChecks.addedInstructions: No new safety instructions, numeric limits, operating sequences, or compliance thresholds added. Existing source cautions retained.
semanticChecks.selfReviewCorrections: Kept explanatory statements declarative and removed an unnecessary container qualifier from one Indonesian prompt.

limitations: Self-review only; no independent peer or native-speaker review. Japanese common name nobiuma is retained as a loanword; scaffold is rendered as plantsa in Tagalog.
